en: Man as an individual relates himself to himself.
He has the twofold side of his particularity and his universal essence.
His duty toward himself is insofar partly his physical preservation, partly [this] to raise his individual being to his universal nature, to form himself.
zh: 人作为个体与自身相关。
他有他的个别性和他的一般本质的双重方面。
他对自己的义务，就此而言一部分是他身体的保存，一部分是［这一点］：把作为个别者的自己提升到其一般本性上去，即进行自我教养。

en: Explanation.
Man is on the one hand a natural being.
As such he behaves according to arbitrariness and chance, as an unstable, subjective being.
He does not distinguish the essential from the non-essential. - Secondly, he is a spiritual, rational being.
According to this side he is not by nature what he should be.
The animal requires no cultivation, for it is by nature what it should be.
It is only a natural being.
Man, however, must bring his twofold side into agreement, make his particularity conform to his rational side, or make the latter the ruling one.

Man is uneducated, for example, when he gives way to his anger and acts blindly in accordance with this affect, because in it he takes an insult or injury to be an infinite injury and seeks to make it up by injuring the offender or other objects without measure and aim. - He is uneducated if someone asserts an interest that is of no concern to him, or in which he can achieve nothing by his activity, since one can sensibly make something one’s interest only where one brings something about by one’s activity. - Further, if man becomes impatient at the encounters of fate, he makes his particular interest into a matter of the highest importance, as something which men and circumstances ought to have accommodated themselves to.
zh: 诠释。
人首先是一个自然存在物。
作为这样的存在物，他按照任意和偶然行事，是一个不稳定的、主观的存在物。
他不把本质性的东西与非本质性的东西区分开来。——其次，他是一个精神的、有理性的存在物。
就这一面而言，他并不是依其本性就是他所应是的东西。
动物不需要教养，因为它依其本性就是它所应是的东西。
它只是一个自然存在物。
但人必须使他的双重方面彼此一致，使他的个别性符合于他理性的一面，或者使后者成为起支配作用的方面。

例如，当人听任自己的怒气发作、盲目地顺着这种情感行事时，他就是未受教养的，因为在这种情况下他把一项侮辱或伤害看成无限的伤害，并且企图不加限度与目标地通过对冒犯者或其他对象的伤害来补偿它。——当某人主张一种与他毫不相干、或者他通过自己的行动根本无法产生效果的利害关系时，他也是未受教养的，因为按理说，人只能在自己通过行动能做成某事的地方，才把那件事变成自己的利害关系。——此外，当人遇到命运的安排而变得不耐烦时，他就把自己特殊的利害关系变成了极其重要的事，好像是人们和情境本应当迁就于它似的。

en: To theoretical cultivation belongs, besides the multiplicity and determinacy of the cognitions and the universality of the viewpoints from which things are to be judged, a sense for the objects in their free independence, without a subjective interest.
zh: 理论的教养除了知识的丰富与规定性、以及据以评判事物的观点的普遍性之外，还包括对对象在其自由独立性方面的感觉，即不带主观的利害关系。

en: Explanation.

The multiplicity of cognitions as such belongs to cultivation, because man thereby raises himself from the particular knowledge of insignificant things of the environment to a general knowledge, through which he attains a greater commonality of knowledge with other men, comes into possession of generally interesting objects.
Insofar as man goes beyond what he immediately knows and experiences, he learns that there are also other and better ways of behaving and acting, and that his own is not the only necessary one.

He withdraws from himself and comes to the distinction of the essential and the non-essential. - The determinacy of cognitions concerns the essential difference of them, the differences that belong to the objects under all circumstances.
To cultivation belongs a judgment about the relations and objects of reality.
For this it is necessary that one know what is at stake, what the nature and the purpose of a thing and of the relations to one another are.
These viewpoints are not given immediately through contemplation, but through occupation with the thing, through reflection on its purpose and essence and on the means, how far the same reach or not.
The uneducated man stays at immediate contemplation.
He has no open eye and does not see what lies before his feet.
It is only a subjective seeing and apprehension.
He does not see the thing.

He knows only roughly what it is like, and not even that correctly, because only the knowledge of the general viewpoints guides to what one must consider essential, or because it already is the most important thing about the thing itself, already contains its most excellent aspects, into which one therefore only has so to speak to lay the external determinate being, and so one is able to apprehend it much more easily and correctly.
zh: 诠释。
知识本身的丰富多样属于教养，因为人由此从对周围无足轻重之物的特殊知识提升到一种普遍知识，通过这种知识他与他人达到更大的知识共同性，并获得对普遍上有趣的对象的占有。
当人越出他直接知道和经历的东西时，他就学到行为与行动还有别的和更好的方式，而他自己那一种并不是唯一必要的方式。
他从自身退开，进而达到对本质性的与非本质性的区分。——知识的规定性涉及它们本质上的差别，即在一切情况下都属于对象的那些差别。
教养还包括对现实性的关系与对象的判断。
为此所需要的是：人应当知道关键何在，知道一件事物以及彼此关系各自的本性和目的是什么。
这些观点并不是通过直观直接给予的，而是通过对该事物的处理、对它的目的与本质以及对其效力所及与否的手段的思考而得到的。
未受教养的人停留在直接直观上。
他没有敞开的眼睛，看不见就在他脚前的东西。
那只是一种主观的观看与把握。
他看不见事情本身。
他只是大致知道这件事物是怎样的，而且连这也并不确切，因为只有对普遍观点的认识才能引向人必须作本质性考察的东西；或者因为它本身就已经是这件事物最主要的东西，已经包含着它最优越的方面，因此人只需要仿佛把外在的定在放进这些方面里去就行，于是也就更能轻易而正确地把握它。

en: The opposite of not knowing how to judge is that one judges hastily about everything without understanding it.
Such a hasty judgment is founded on the fact that one does indeed grasp a viewpoint, but a one-sided one, and thereby overlooks the true concept of the thing, the remaining viewpoints.
A cultivated man also knows the limit of his judgement.
zh: 与「不懂得判断」相反的，是不加理解就对一切匆忙下判断。
这种匆忙的判断建立在这样一点上：人确实抓住了一个观点，却是一个片面的观点，因而就忽略了事情真正的概念、忽略了其余的观点。
一个有教养的人同时知道自己判断能力的界限。

en: Furthermore, to cultivation belongs a sense for the objective in its freedom.

It lies in this, that I do not seek my particular subject in the object, but consider and treat the objects as they are in and for themselves in their free peculiarity, that I take an interest in them without a particular benefit. - Such an unselfish interest lies in the study of the sciences, namely when one cultivates them for their own sake.
The desire to draw benefit from the objects of nature is connected with their destruction. - The interest in beautiful art is also an unselfish one.

It represents things in their living independence and leaves out the paltry and stunted as they suffer from external circumstances. - The objective action consists in this, that 1. it also has with respect to its indifferent side the form of the universal, free of arbitrariness, mood and caprice, from the extraordinary and the like; 2. with respect to its inner, essential side it is objective when one has the true thing itself as one’s purpose, without self-interested interest.
zh: 此外，教养还包括对客观事物之自由的感受力。
它在于：我不去对象中寻找我的特殊主体，而是按照对象自在自为的样子、在它们自由的特性上去观察和处理它们，也就是说不带任何特殊的利益去关心它们。——这样的无私兴趣就在对科学的研究中：当人正是为科学自身而研究它的时候。
要从自然的对象中谋取利益的欲求，是与它们的破坏联系在一起的。——对美的艺术感兴趣同样是一种无私的兴趣。
它把事物以其活的独立性表现出来，并把那些因外在情境而受损的贫乏与萎缩之物略去。——客观的行为在于：1. 它即使就其无所谓的一面而言也具有普遍者的形式，摆脱了任意、情绪和怪癖，摆脱了特殊之类的东西；2. 就其内在的、本质的一面而言，当人把事情的真身本身当作自己的目的而不带自利的利害关系时，它就是客观的。

en: To practical cultivation belongs that man show that composure and moderation in the satisfaction of natural needs and drives which lies within the limits of their necessity, namely self-preservation.

He must 1. be free of the natural, of it; 2. on the contrary, in his vocation, in the essential, he must be [deeply engaged], and therefore 3. he must be able not only to restrict the satisfaction of the natural to the limits of necessity, but also to sacrifice it to higher duties.
zh: 实践的教养包括：人在满足自然的需求与冲动时，表现出那种处在其必然性的界限之内、亦即自我保存的清醒与节制。
他必须 1. 从自然的东西中走出来，摆脱它；2. 相反，在自己的职业中、在本质性的事情上，他必须深入，并且因此 3. 不仅要把对自然之物的满足限制在必然性的界限之内，还要能够把它牺牲给更高的义务。

en: Explanation.

Man’s freedom from natural drives does not consist in the fact that he has none and so does not strive to escape his nature, but in the fact that he acknowledges them as such as something necessary and thereby rational and accomplishes them accordingly with his will.
He finds himself compelled in this only insofar as he sets up random and arbitrary impulses and purposes against the universal.
The determinate, exact measure in the satisfaction of needs and in the use of physical and spiritual powers cannot be indicated exactly, but everyone can know what is useful or harmful to him.

Moderation in the satisfaction of natural drives and in the use of bodily powers is necessary as such for the sake of health, for health is an essential condition for the use of spiritual powers for the fulfillment of man’s higher determination.

If the body is not preserved in its ordinary condition, if it is injured in one of its functions, one must make it the purpose of one’s activity, whereby it becomes something dangerous and significant for the spirit. - Furthermore, exceeding the measure in the use of physical and spiritual powers has as a consequence, either through too much or too little, a blunting and weakening of them.
zh: 诠释。
人摆脱自然冲动的自由，不在于他没有自然冲动、因而不谋求逃离自己的本性，而在于他总体上把它们承认为某种必然的、因而也是合乎理性的东西，并以自己的意志相应地完成它们。
他只在把偶然的和任意的念头与目的同普遍者相对立这一点上，才感到自己受约束。
在满足需求和使用身体与精神力量时那个确定而精确的分寸，是无法精确指出的，但每个人都能知道什么对自己有益、什么有害。
在满足自然冲动和使用身体力量时的节制，总体上出于健康的缘故是必要的，因为健康是运用精神力量以实现人的更高规定的一个本质条件。
如果身体没有保持在它的正常状态、如果它的某一项功能受到损害，人就必须把身体当作自己活动的目的，这样它就成为对精神来说某种危险而重大的东西。——此外，在使用身体与精神力量时越过分寸，无论是过多还是过少，都会导致这些力量的迟钝与虚弱。

en: Finally, moderation is connected with composure.

This consists in the consciousness of what one does, that man surveys himself through his reflection in the enjoyment or in the work, and so is not wholly surrendered to this individual state, but remains open to the consideration of something else, which may also still be necessary.
In composure one is out of one’s state, of the sensation or of the business, together with the spirit.
This position of not sinking completely into one’s state is as such required with regard to drives and purposes which are indeed necessary but not essential in the process.
On the contrary, with regard to a true purpose or business the spirit must be present with its whole earnestness and not at the same time be outside of it.
Composure here consists in one’s having all the circumstances and sides of the work before one’s eyes.
zh: 最后，节制与清醒是相联系的。
这种清醒在于对自己正在做的事有所意识：人在享受或工作中通过反思审视自己，因此并不完全沉溺于这一个别的状态，而是对「别的东西——它也许同样还是必要的」保持敞开。
在清醒中，人连同精神一起，从自己的状态、从感觉或从所办之事中抽身出来。
这种「不完全沉入自己状态」的姿态，总体上对于那些固然必要、但在此过程中并非本质性的冲动和目的来说是必需的。
相反，对于真正的目的或事业，精神必须以全部的认真在场，而不能同时又置身于它之外。
这里的清醒在于：人把工作的一切情境和各个侧面都看在眼里。

en: As for the determinate vocation which appears as a fate, the form of an external necessity is to be lifted from it as such.
One is to take it up with freedom and to endure and carry it out in such freedom.
zh: 至于那个显得像是命运的规定了的职业，总体上要扬弃掉加在它身上的外在必然性的形式。
要用自由去着手于它，并以这样的自由去坚持和完成它。

en: Explanation.

Man, with a view to the external circumstances of fate and to everything of which he is at all immediately the being, must behave in such a way that he makes the same his own, that he takes from it the form of an external determinate being.
It does not depend in which external state man finds himself through fate, if he is right in what he is, i.e. if he fills out all sides of his vocation.
The vocation to an estate is a many-sided substance.
It is as it were a stuff or material which he must work through in all directions, so that it has in it nothing alien, brittle, and resistant.
Insofar as I have made it completely mine for myself, I am free in it.
Man is especially discontented when he does not fill out his vocation.
He gives himself a relation which he does not truly have as his own.
At the same time he belongs to this estate.
He cannot rid himself of it.
He thus lives and acts in a relation with himself that is contrary to his will.
zh: 诠释。
就命运的外部情境以及他直接所是的一切而言，人必须这样行事：他把它变成自己的东西，他从中取消了外在定在的形式。
人在命运中处于哪一种外在状态并不重要，只要他把自己所是的东西做对，即只要他把自己职业的所有方面都填满。
一个提升到某种地位的职业是一种多方面的实体。
它仿佛是一种材料，他必须朝各个方向把它彻底加工透，好使它其中不再有任何陌生的、脆硬的和抵触的东西。
只要我已把它完完全全地变成我自己的东西，我就在其中是自由的。
人在没有填满自己的职业时，特别会感到不满。
他给自己一个关系，而他并没有真正把它当作自己的东西。
同时他又属于这个地位。
他无法从中摆脱出来。
于是他就生活在并行动于一种令他自己反感的自我关系之中。

en: Fidelity and obedience in one’s vocation, as well as obedience toward fate and self-forgetfulness in one’s acting, have as their ground the giving up of vanity, self-conceit and self-seeking against what is in and for itself and necessary.
zh: 职业中的忠诚与服从、对命运的服从以及行动中的自我遗忘，其根据在于放弃那虚荣、自负与自私对自在自为而必然之物的抗拒。

en: Explanation.
The vocation is something universal and necessary and makes up some side of human life in common.
It is thus a part of the whole work of humanity.
When man has a vocation, he enters into participation and cooperation in the universal.
He thereby becomes something objective.
The vocation is indeed a single, limited sphere, yet it makes up a necessary member of the whole and is also in itself again a whole.
If man is to become something, he must know how to limit himself, i.e. to make his vocation entirely his concern.
Then it is no limitation for him.
He is then at one with himself, with his externality, with his sphere.

He is something universal, a whole. - If man makes something vain to himself, i.e. something non-essential and trivial, his purpose, then what lies at the basis here is not an interest in a thing but in his own thing.
The vain is nothing existing in and for itself, but is preserved only through the subject.

Man sees in this only himself; e.g. there can also be a moral vanity when man in his acting is at all conscious of his excellence and has the interest more in himself than in the thing. - The man who faithfully accomplishes small tasks shows himself capable of greater ones, because he has shown obedience, a giving up of his wishes, inclinations, and fancies.
zh: 诠释。
职业是某种普遍而必然的东西，它构成人共同生活中的一面。
所以它是整个人类作品的一部分。
当人有了职业，他就是参与并协作于普遍者。
他由此成为一个客观的东西。
职业固然是一个个别的、受限制的领域，但它构成整体的一个必要环节，而且它自身又是一个整体。
如果人应当成为某种东西，他就必须懂得限制自己，也就是完完全全地把自己的职业当作自己的事情。
那么它对他就不再是界限。
于是他就与自身、与他的外在性、与他的领域合而为一。
他是一个普遍者、一个整体。——当人把某种虚妄的东西，即某种非本质的、琐屑的东西当作自己的目的时，这时所依据的并不是对某件事物的利害关系，而是对他自己的事情的利害关系。
虚妄的东西并不是自在自为地存在着的东西，而只是靠主体才得以维持。
人在其中只看见自己；例如，也可能有道德上的虚荣：当人在行动中总体上意识到自己的卓越，而把利害关系更多地放在自己而非事情上时。——那个忠实地完成小事的人表明自己有能力完成更大的事，因为他表现出了服从，表现出了对自己的愿望、倾向和幻想的放弃。

en: Through intellectual and moral cultivation man acquires the ability to fulfil the duties toward others, which duties can be called real, whereas the duties that relate to cultivation are more of a formal nature.
zh: 通过智性的与道德的教养，人获得履行对他人的义务的能力；这些义务可以称为实在的义务，而那些关涉教养的义务则更具形式的性质。

en: Insofar as the fulfilment of duties appears more as the subjective property of an individual and belongs more to his natural character, it is virtue.
zh: 就义务的履行显得更是一个个体的主观财产、更属于他的自然性情而言，它就是美德。

en: Because virtue is partly connected with the natural character, it appears as a morality of a determinate kind and of greater liveliness and intensity.
At the same time it is less bound up with the consciousness of duty than morality proper.
zh: 由于美德部分地与自然性情相连，它显得是一种特定样式的道德，并且具有更大的生动性与强度。
同时它同义务意识的联系，也不如道德本身那样紧密。

en: Insofar as man is cultivated, he has the possibility of acting.
Insofar as he really acts, he is necessarily in relation with other men.
The first necessary relation in which the individual enters into relation with others is the family relation.
It indeed also has a legal side, but it is subordinated to the side of moral disposition, of love, and of trust.
zh: 就人受过教养而言，他就有行动的可能。
就他真正行动而言，他必然处于与他人���关系之中。
个体与他人发生关系的第一种必然关系，就是家庭关系。
它固然也有一面法的方面，但这一面从属于道德心态、爱的和信任的那一面。

en: Explanation.
The family essentially makes up only one substance, only one person.
The family members are not persons toward one another.
They enter into such a relation only insofar as the moral bond has been dissolved through a misfortune.
Among the ancients the disposition of family love, acting in its sense, was called pietas.

Pietas has in common with Frömmigkeit, which is also designated by this word, that it presupposes an absolute bond, the unity existing in and for itself in a spiritual substance, a bond that is not tied by particular arbitrariness or chance.
zh: 诠释。
家庭本质上只构成一个实体，只构成一个人格。
家庭成员彼此之间并不是各自独立的人格。
只有当道德的纽带因一场不幸而解开时，他们才进入这样的关系。
在古人那里，家庭之爱的这种心态、按它的意义行事，叫做 pietas。
孝敬与虔诚——后者也用同一个词来称呼——的共同之处在于：它们都预设一条绝对的纽带，即在一个精神实体中自在自为地存在的统一，一条不是由特殊的任意或偶然系在一起的纽带。

en: This disposition consists more precisely in the fact that every member of the family does not have its essence in its own person, but that only the whole of the family constitutes their personality.
zh: 这种心态更确切地说在于：家庭的每一个成员并不把自身的本质置于自身的人格之中，而唯有家庭的整体才构成他们的人格性。

en: The union of persons of the two sexes, which is marriage, is essentially neither merely a natural, animal union nor a mere civil contract, but a moral union of disposition in mutual love and trust, which makes them into one person.
zh: 异性人格之间的结合即是婚姻，它本质上既不只是自然的、兽性的结合，也不只是纯粹的民事契约，而是心态在相互的爱与信任中的一种道德的结合，这种结合使他们成为一个人格。

en: The duty of parents toward children is to provide for their preservation and education, - that of children [to obey them] until they become independent, and to honor them their whole life, - that of siblings as such, to act toward one another according to love and special equity.
zh: 父母对子女的义务是为他们的保存与教育操劳，——子女的义务则是［服从］他们直到自己独立自主为止，并终其一生敬重他们，——兄弟姐妹之间的义务，总的说来，是按爱和格外的公平彼此行事。

en: The natural whole which the family constitutes expands into the whole of a people and a state, in which the individuals have an independent will of their own.
zh: 家庭所构成的这个自然整体，扩展为一个民族和国家的整体；在其中，各个人各自具有独立的意志。

en: Explanation.
The state on the one hand aims at being able to do without the disposition of the citizens, namely insofar as it has to make itself independent of the will of the individuals.
It therefore prescribes precisely their liabilities to the individuals, namely the share which they must perform for the whole.

It cannot rely on disposition alone, because that can just as well be self-interested and can oppose the interest of the state. - In this way the state becomes a machine, a system of external dependencies.
But on the other hand it cannot do without the disposition of the citizens.
The prescription of the government can contain only what is general.
The actual action, the fulfilment of the state’s purposes, contains the particular mode of efficacy.
This can only arise from the individual understanding, from the disposition of man.
zh: 诠释。
国家一方面力求能够不依赖公民的心态，也就是就它必须使自己独立于各个人的意志而言。
所以它准确地规定各个人的责任，也就是他们必须为整体付出的份额。
它不能只依赖心态，因为心态同样可以是自利的，并且可以与国家的利益相对立。——以这种方式，国家就成为一台机器、一个外在依赖的系统。
但另一方面，它也不能没有公民的心态。
政府的训令只能包含普遍的东西。
现实的行动、国家目的之实现，包含着起作用的具体方式。
这只能出自个人的知性、出自人的心态。

en: The state comprehends society not only under legal relations but, as a genuinely higher moral community, mediates the unity in customs, cultivation, and general mode of thinking and acting (in that each surveys and recognizes his own universality in the other in a spiritual way).
zh: 国家不仅在法的关系之下把握社会，而且作为一个真正更高的道德共同体，在习俗、教养以及一般的思维与行动方式上促成一致性（每个人在他人身上以精神的方式观照并认出他自身的普遍性）。

en: In the spirit of a people each single citizen has his spiritual substance.

The preservation of the individuals is founded not only on the preservation of this living whole, but this same whole also constitutes the general spiritual nature or the essence of each one against his particularity.
The preservation of the whole therefore precedes the preservation of the individual, and all shall have this disposition.
zh: 在一个民族的精神中，每一个公民都有他的精神实体。
各个人的保存不仅建立在这个活的整体的保存之上，而且正是这个整体，使每个人那普遍的精神本性、或者其本质，得以抵挡他的个别性。
所以整体的保存先于个人的保存，并且所有人都应当具有这种心态。

en: Considered purely with respect to its legal side, insofar as the state protects the private rights of the individuals and the individual first looks to what is his own, a sacrifice of a part of property against the state is indeed possible in order to preserve the rest.
Patriotism, however, is not founded on this calculation but on the consciousness of the absoluteness of the state.

This disposition, to sacrifice property and life for the whole, is all the greater in a people the more the individuals can act for the whole with their own will and self-activity, and the greater trust they have in it.
(The beautiful patriotism of the Greeks. - Distinction of Bürger as bourgeois and citoyen.)
zh: 单从法的方面看，就国家保护各个人的私权、而个人首先着眼于自己所有的东西而言，为了保住其余部分，对国家牺牲一部分财产确实是可能的。
但爱国主义并不建立在这种计算之上，而是建立在对国家之绝对性的意识之上。
这种为整体牺牲财产与生命的心态，在一个民族中越是各个个能以自己的意志和自主活动为整体行事、并且越是他们对它抱有更大的信任，就越是伟大。
（希腊人的高贵爱国主义。——「Bürger」作为 bourgeois 与 citoyen 的差别。）

en: The disposition of obedience toward the commands of the government, of attachment to the person of the prince and to the constitution, and the feeling of national honour are the virtues of the citizen of every well-ordered state.
zh: 服从政府命令的心态、对君主本人和对宪法的依恋之情以及民族荣誉感，是一个秩序良好的国家的公民的美德。

en: The state does not rest on an express contract of one with all and of all with one, or of the individual with the government; and the general will of the whole is not the expressing will of the individuals but is the absolutely general will which is binding for the individuals in and for itself.
zh: 国家并不建立在「一人与所有人、所有人与一人」或「个人与政府」之间的明文契约之上；并且整体那普遍意志并不是各个人的表达出来的意志，而是自在自为地对各个具有约束力的绝对普遍的意志。

en: The duties toward others are first the legal duties, which must be bound up with the disposition to do right for the sake of right.

The remaining of these duties are founded on the disposition to hold others equal to oneself not only as abstract person but also in their particularity, to consider their weal and woe as one’s own, and to prove this by active help.
zh: 对他人的义务首先是法权义务，它们必须与「为了权利本身而去做」的心态相联结。
这些义务中的其余各项，建立在这样一种心态上：不把他人仅仅当作抽象的人格，而且也当其特殊性而与自己同等看待，把他们的福祉与祸患当作自己的，并通过积极的帮助来证明这一点。

en: This moral way of thinking and acting goes beyond right.
Rectitude, however, the observance of the strict duties toward others, is the first duty which must underlie.
There can be noble and generous actions which are without rectitude.
They then have their ground in self-love and in the consciousness of having done something special, whereas what rectitude demands is a duty valid for all, not an arbitrary one.
zh: 这种道德的思维与行动方式超出了法。
但正直，即对他人严格义务的遵守，是必须作为基础的第一项义务。
可以有高尚而豪爽的行为是不带正直的。
它们于是以自爱和「自己做了点特别的事」这一意识为根据；而正直所要求的则是一项对所有人都有效、并非出于任意的义务。

en: Among the particular duties toward others, truthfulness in speaking and acting is the first.

It consists in the equality of what is and what one is conscious of with that which one expresses and shows toward others. - Untruthfulness is the inequality and the contradiction of the consciousness and of that which one is for others, thus of one’s inner and one’s actuality, and thereby the nullity of oneself.
zh: 在对他人的特殊义务中，言说与行动上的真实性是第一项。
它在于：所是的东西和所意识的东西，同对他人所表达和所显示的东西彼此等同。——不真实则是意识与「自己对于他人是怎样的」之间的不等同与矛盾，因而是自己的内在与自己的现实性之间的不等同与矛盾，并由此成为自身的虚无性。

en: Untruthfulness also belongs pre-eminently to the case in which what one means is supposed to be a good intention or disposition, whereas what one does is something evil.

(This inequality between the disposition and what the action is in itself would at least be a clumsiness, but insofar as the actor is at all guilty, one must take such a one who does evil to mean it as evil too.)
zh: 不真实尤其还包括这样一种情形：一个人心里以为自己是出于好的意图或心态，而他做的事却是恶的。
（这种心态与行为本身之所是之间的不等同，至少还算是一种不灵巧；但就行动者总之有罪责而言，一个做恶事的人必须被认为也是怀着恶念去做它的。）

en: It presupposes a particular relation in order to have the right to tell someone the truth about his conduct.
If one does this without having the right to it, then one is untruthful in that one sets up a relation to the other which does not hold.
zh: 它预设一种特殊的关系，才能有权利把某人的行为举止的真情告诉对方。
如果人这样做而并不具有这种权利，那么他就是不真实的，因为他对对方建立起一种并不成立的关系。

en: Explanation.
For a first thing it is the first thing to say the truth insofar as one knows that it is true.
It is ignoble not to say the truth when it is in its right place to say it, because one thereby degrades oneself before oneself and before the other.
But one also ought not to say the truth when one has no calling for it or not even a right.

If one merely says the truth in order to have done one’s duty, without further success, then it is at least something superfluous, for the point is not that I have said the matter, but that it comes about.
Speaking is not yet the deed or action, which is higher. - The truth is then said in the right place and at the right time when it serves to bring the matter about.
Speech is a remarkably great means, but great understanding is required to use it correctly.
zh: 诠释。
首先，应当说出真相，就人知道它是真实的而言。
在该说真话的地方不说真话，是不高贵的，因为人由此在自己和他人面前贬低了自己。
但如果人对此没有职责、乃至没有权利，也不应当说真话。
如果人说出真相只是为了尽了自己的责任、却没有进一步的效果，那么这至少是一件多余的事，因为关键不在于我说了这件事，而在于事情得以实现。
言说还不是那更高的行为或行动。——当说真话有助于使事情得以实现时，真相就是在恰当的地方、在恰当的时候被说出的。
言说是一个大得出奇的手段，但要正确地使用它，则需要很大的知性。

en: With defamation, which is a real lie, is connected the evil speaking about others, the narration of such things as are detrimental to the honour of a third person and are not manifest to the narrator in and for themselves.
It is accustomed to happen in disapproving zeal against unmoral actions, even with the addition that one could not vouch for the narrations for certain and would have meant to say nothing.

But in this case it is connected with dishonesty, actually spreading the narrations one professes not to want to spread; and in the other case with hypocrisy, wanting to speak morally and actually acting evilly.
zh: 与诽谤——一种真正的谎话——相联系的是恶言中伤，即讲述那些有损于第三者名誉、并且对讲述者本人并非自在自为地显而易见的事情。
这种情形常以义愤的形式针对不合道德的行为发生，甚至还会附带一句：这些讲述不能确定担保，而且自己并没有说什么。
但在前一种情形中，这与不诚实相连：口称不想散播这些讲述，实际上却散播了它们；在后一种情形中，则与伪善相连：想要说道德的话，实际上却做着恶事。
